question: In an ordinary four-player curling game, our team has last stone and neither team scores in the end. Who keeps last-stone advantage next end, and how does that differ from us scoring one point?
generated_answer:
In a four-player game, if neither team scores in an end, the team with last stone in the previous end retains last stone advantage for the next end. This is because the game continues with the same team having last stone until they score or the other team scores.

However, if your team scores one point in the end, the last-stone advantage switches to the other team for the next end. This is because scoring a point means you've successfully delivered a stone into the house, and the other team now has last stone.

So, if neither team scores, you keep last stone. If you score, the other team gets last stone. If the other team scores, they keep last stone. The last-stone advantage is only transferred when a team scores or when the game starts with no previous end (like the first end of the game).

In summary, if neither team scores, you keep last stone. If you score, the other team gets last stone. If they score, they keep last stone. This is the standard rule in curling, regardless of the number of players. 

For more information, you can refer to the official World Curling Federation rules, specifically Rule 3 (The Game) and Rule 4 (The End).
